reading.title: The Science of Honesty
reading.intro_zh: 课文讲的是良心与归还失物；这篇拓展阅读改写自一项发表在《科学》(Science) 杂志、由密歇根大学等机构开展的全球“丢钱包”实验，用真实数据揭示人为什么会把别人的钱还回来。

source.title: Moral concerns override desire to profit from finding a lost wallet (Cohn et al., Science, 2019)

passage: Would you return a stranger's lost wallet, especially if it were stuffed with cash? Economists once assumed that the more money a wallet contained, the greater the temptation to keep it. A landmark experiment published in the journal Science overturned that intuition. Researchers deliberately handed in 17,303 "lost" wallets to banks, museums, post offices and police stations across 355 cities in 40 countries, then quietly recorded whether each one was reported to its supposed owner.

The results were strikingly counterintuitive. Empty wallets were returned only about 40 per cent of the time, yet wallets holding a modest sum were reported in 51 per cent of cases, and those bulging with roughly ninety dollars came back 72 per cent of the time. In thirty-eight of the forty countries surveyed, the presence of more cash actually raised, rather than lowered, the likelihood of an honest return. Rates varied widely between nations, with Switzerland, Norway and the Netherlands among the most scrupulous.

Why would temptation produce honesty? The investigators concluded that the decisive factor was psychological rather than financial. Pocketing a wallet thick with money forces people to confront an uncomfortable self-image: that of a thief. Because most of us are reluctant to revise our view of ourselves as decent, the internal cost of dishonesty climbs as the stolen amount rises. In other words, conscience, not the fear of punishment, did the heavy lifting. Honesty, the authors argue, is sustained less by external surveillance than by the quiet desire to remain, in our own eyes, a trustworthy person.

questions.question: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Wallets are most often lost in banks, museums and police stations.
Honesty is mainly enforced by the fear of being caught and punished.
A global experiment found that people returned wallets containing more money more often, driven by conscience.
Switzerland and Norway have the strictest laws against keeping lost property.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文主线是：一项全球“丢钱包”实验发现，钱越多反而越可能被归还，原因是良心而非外部惩罚。选项C概括了这一核心。

questions.question: How large was the experiment described in the passage?
options: 17,303 wallets were handed in across 355 cities in 40 countries.
Exactly 40 wallets were tested in a single Swiss city.
About ninety wallets were left in banks and museums worldwide.
355 wallets were mailed to police stations in 17 countries.
questions.explanation_zh: 第一段明确写道：研究者上交了 17,303 个“丢失”的钱包，分布在 40 个国家的 355 座城市，所以选项A正确。

questions.question: According to the researchers, why did wallets with more money come back more often?
options: Because larger wallets were easier for staff to notice and store.
Because the law punishes the theft of large sums far more severely.
Because people hoped to receive a bigger reward for returning them.
Because keeping a great deal of money would force people to see themselves as thieves.
questions.explanation_zh: 第三段解释：拿走装满钱的钱包会迫使人面对“自己是小偷”这一自我形象，金额越大，不诚实的内心代价越高，因此更可能归还。选项D对应。

questions.question: What can we infer about human honesty from the study's conclusion?
options: People are honest only when cameras or guards are watching them.
For many people, the wish to keep a good self-image matters more than the money itself.
Honesty disappears completely once the sum involved becomes very large.
Financial reward is the single strongest reason people return lost property.
questions.explanation_zh: 作者总结诚实更多源于“想在自己眼中保持可信赖形象”的内心愿望，而非外部监督，可推断对许多人而言良好的自我形象比金钱更重要，故选B。

questions.question: In the passage, the word "scrupulous" most nearly means
options: wealthy and generous with strangers.
suspicious of other people's motives.
careful to behave honestly and do what is right.
indifferent to whether money is returned.
questions.explanation_zh: “scrupulous”指做事一丝不苟、严守道德、诚实正直。文中说瑞士、挪威、荷兰是“among the most scrupulous”，即归还率最高、最讲诚信，故选C。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把五个 Lesson 45 的“匿名归还”句式提升到 B2+：用 had been lost 写之前已经丢失，用 while taking 交代背景动作，用 must have been found 对过去做强推测，用 had been wrapped up...and contained... 描写被送回的物件，最后用 In time...was paid back 写一笔钱终于被还清。试着把它们用到更抽象、更正式的语境里。

patterns.title: a large sum of money had been lost
patterns.source: A large sum of money had been lost.
patterns.focus_zh: had been lost 是被动 + 过去完成，强调“在那之前钱已经丢了”，重点在丢失这件事，而不是谁弄丢的。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：在一次审计、核对或事故被发现之前，一笔款项、一批数据或一份重要档案“早已不知去向”，用 had been lost 突出丢失这一既成结果。
patterns.sample: By the time the auditors finished their review, a startling sum of donated money had been lost without any clear record of where it went.
patterns.tip_zh: had been + 过去分词 是被动；它发生在另一个过去时间点之前，所以用 had。

patterns.title: while taking ...
patterns.source: Sam Benton had lost his wallet while taking his savings to the post office.
patterns.focus_zh: while taking... 表示“正在做某事的时候”，用来交代事情发生时的背景动作。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：某人在执行一项有责任的任务（while taking...，比如运送、保管或交接某物）的过程中，意外地弄丢、损坏或泄露了重要东西。
patterns.sample: The young cashier accidentally dropped an envelope of takings while taking the day's earnings down to the night safe.
patterns.tip_zh: while taking 后面接正在进行的背景动作，主句再写真正发生的事。

patterns.title: must have been found by ...
patterns.source: The wallet must have been found by one of the villagers.
patterns.focus_zh: must have been found 是对过去的强推测：说话人没看见，但很确定某样东西一定被某人找到了。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：面对一件你没有亲眼目睹的离奇消失或出现，根据线索做出强烈推断——某样东西过去一定已经被某个人发现或取走。
patterns.sample: Since the documents had vanished overnight, the manager concluded they must have been found and quietly removed by an insider.
patterns.tip_zh: must have been + 过去分词 = 对过去的强烈推测，比 maybe 更肯定。

patterns.title: It had been wrapped up ... and contained ...
patterns.source: It had been wrapped up in newspaper and it contained half the money.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 had been wrapped up 写它被包起来，用 contained 写里面装着什么，一起描述一件被送回来的东西。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：描写一个被匿名送回或意外发现的包裹、信封或盒子——它被什么样的东西包裹着，里面又完整地装着什么。
patterns.sample: The anonymous package left at reception had been wrapped up in plain brown paper and contained the entire missing fund, down to the last coin.
patterns.tip_zh: had been wrapped up 说“被包好了”，contained 说“里面有”，两个动词分工不同。

patterns.title: In time, ... was paid back
patterns.source: In time, all Sam's money was paid back in this way.
patterns.focus_zh: In time 表示“经过一段时间，终于”，was paid back 是被动，一起写出一笔钱最终被还清。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一笔被挪用、拖欠或丢失的款项，经过一段时间后终于被全部还清，并暗示金钱之外仍有难以弥补的代价。
patterns.sample: In time, every penny of the misappropriated grant was paid back, though the trust it had broken proved far harder to restore.
patterns.tip_zh: In time 不是“准时”，而是“最终、过了一段时间以后”；was paid back 强调钱被还回来的结果。
